summary: This program defines a RobotPet class, a blueprint for creating robot pet objects that each carry a name, a battery level, and a mood. It then creates three distinct pets and prints each one's attributes.

lines.text: This is the constructor, a special method Python runs automatically whenever a new RobotPet is created. The arguments after self are the pieces of information you must supply about the pet.
The argument name only exists while the constructor runs; assigning it to self.name stores it on the pet object itself so it can be read back later. The same pattern saves battery and mood.

Calling the class like a function builds one pet in a single line, and the arguments are matched to the constructor's parameters in order. This is what makes creating many unique pets so much less work than writing a dictionary for each.
Dot notation reads an attribute back off a particular object, so pet1.name is Rover's name and never Sparky's. Each pet keeps its own separate copy of the three attributes.
